title: Surprisingly Complex Waves Reveal the Brain's Inner Workings
title_zh: 令人惊讶的复杂波揭示大脑内部工作机制

paragraphs.en: I get out of bed. I walk through the dimly lit hallway, thinking of what’s in my fridge and what I should have for breakfast. With no real effort, I’ve navigated my environment, accessed my memory, and assessed the energetic state of my body, all in the space of a few seconds. How is the brain able to do this?
paragraphs.zh: 我从床上起来。 我走过灯光昏暗的走廊，想着冰箱里有什么、早餐该吃什么。 毫不费力地，我就在短短几秒钟内完成了对环境的导航、对记忆的提取，以及对身体能量状态的评估。 大脑是如何做到这一切的？

sents.en: I get out of bed.
sents.zh: 我从床上起来。

sents.en: I walk through the dimly lit hallway, thinking of what’s in my fridge and what I should have for breakfast.
sents.zh: 我走过灯光昏暗的走廊，想着冰箱里有什么、早餐该吃什么。

sents.en: With no real effort, I’ve navigated my environment, accessed my memory, and assessed the energetic state of my body, all in the space of a few seconds.
sents.zh: 毫不费力地，我就在短短几秒钟内完成了对环境的导航、对记忆的提取，以及对身体能量状态的评估。

sents.en: How is the brain able to do this?
sents.zh: 大脑是如何做到这一切的？

paragraphs.en: Partly by harnessing electricity. The brain spends about half of its energetic resources maintaining the electrochemical gradients that keep neurons poised and ready to fire at a moment’s notice. This gives the brain an extraordinary level of flexibility in responding to the demands of everyday life. The collective electrical activity of many neurons can be seen as waves propagating through the brain from one region to the next, like the raised arms of enthusiastic spectators at a football game.
paragraphs.zh: 部分是通过利用电来实现的。 大脑将大约一半的能量用于维持电化学梯度，使神经元时刻保持待命状态，随时可以发放。 这使大脑在应对日常生活的需求时具有非凡的灵活性。 许多神经元的集体电活动可以被视为在大脑中从一个区域传播到下一个区域的波，就像足球比赛上热情观众掀起的人浪一样。

sents.en: Partly by harnessing electricity.
sents.zh: 部分是通过利用电来实现的。

sents.en: The brain spends about half of its energetic resources maintaining the electrochemical gradients that keep neurons poised and ready to fire at a moment’s notice.
sents.zh: 大脑将大约一半的能量用于维持电化学梯度，使神经元时刻保持待命状态，随时可以发放。

sents.en: This gives the brain an extraordinary level of flexibility in responding to the demands of everyday life.
sents.zh: 这使大脑在应对日常生活的需求时具有非凡的灵活性。

sents.en: The collective electrical activity of many neurons can be seen as waves propagating through the brain from one region to the next, like the raised arms of enthusiastic spectators at a football game.
sents.zh: 许多神经元的集体电活动可以被视为在大脑中从一个区域传播到下一个区域的波，就像足球比赛上热情观众掀起的人浪一样。

paragraphs.en: New lines of research are revealing that these waves are more complex than previously known. Typically measured by electrodes, they have been identified as basic planar waves: simply structured oscillations in neural activity. Neuroscientists have traditionally interpreted this as a bit like the sound of the brain’s engine revving, little more than a sign that it’s working. However, emerging evidence in humans and animals suggests that traveling waves play a central role in how the brain functions.
paragraphs.zh: 新的研究方向正在揭示，这些波比以往所知的更为复杂。 这些波通常通过电极来测量，此前被认为是一种基本的平面波：结构简单的神经活动振荡。 神经科学家传统上将其解读为有点像大脑引擎的轰鸣声，仅仅表明大脑在运转而已。 然而，来自人类和动物研究的新兴证据表明，行波在大脑的运作方式中发挥着核心作用。

sents.en: New lines of research are revealing that these waves are more complex than previously known.
sents.zh: 新的研究方向正在揭示，这些波比以往所知的更为复杂。

sents.en: Typically measured by electrodes, they have been identified as basic planar waves: simply structured oscillations in neural activity.
sents.zh: 这些波通常通过电极来测量，此前被认为是一种基本的平面波：结构简单的神经活动振荡。

sents.en: Neuroscientists have traditionally interpreted this as a bit like the sound of the brain’s engine revving, little more than a sign that it’s working.
sents.zh: 神经科学家传统上将其解读为有点像大脑引擎的轰鸣声，仅仅表明大脑在运转而已。

sents.en: However, emerging evidence in humans and animals suggests that traveling waves play a central role in how the brain functions.
sents.zh: 然而，来自人类和动物研究的新兴证据表明，行波在大脑的运作方式中发挥着核心作用。

paragraphs.en: “The work coming out is moving this from ‘Are they relevant?’ to ‘This is a major motif of how the cortex processes information,’” said Earl K. Miller , a cognitive neuroscientist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
paragraphs.zh: “这项研究正把这个问题从‘它们是否相关？’推进到‘这是大脑皮层处理信息的一个主要主题’，”麻省理工学院的认知神经科学家厄尔·K·米勒说道。

paragraphs.en: In a study published in April 2026 in Nature Communications , neuroscientists measured traveling waves of neural activity and observed a menagerie: source waves that appear to emanate from one location, sink waves that converge on a spot, and vortexlike spiral waves. The team, which included Joshua Jacobs and Anup Das from the University of Chicago, found that different behavioral tasks were associated with distinct wave patterns.
paragraphs.zh: 在2026年4月发表于《自然·通讯》（Nature Communications）的一项研究中，神经科学家测量了神经活动的行进波，并观察到了各种各样的波形：似乎从某一位置发出的源波、汇聚到某一点的汇波，以及类似旋涡的螺旋波。 该研究团队包括芝加哥大学的约书亚·雅各布斯（Joshua Jacobs）和阿努普·达斯（Anup Das），他们发现不同的行为任务与不同的波形模式相关联。

sents.en: In a study published in April 2026 in Nature Communications , neuroscientists measured traveling waves of neural activity and observed a menagerie: source waves that appear to emanate from one location, sink waves that converge on a spot, and vortexlike spiral waves.
sents.zh: 在2026年4月发表于《自然·通讯》（Nature Communications）的一项研究中，神经科学家测量了神经活动的行进波，并观察到了各种各样的波形：似乎从某一位置发出的源波、汇聚到某一点的汇波，以及类似旋涡的螺旋波。

sents.en: The team, which included Joshua Jacobs and Anup Das from the University of Chicago, found that different behavioral tasks were associated with distinct wave patterns.
sents.zh: 该研究团队包括芝加哥大学的约书亚·雅各布斯（Joshua Jacobs）和阿努普·达斯（Anup Das），他们发现不同的行为任务与不同的波形模式相关联。

paragraphs.en: Joshua Jacobs and Anup Das were part of a team that observed complex patterns of brain waves using intracranial electrodes.
paragraphs.zh: Joshua Jacobs 和 Anup Das 是一个团队的成员，该团队使用颅内电极观察到了复杂的脑电波模式。

paragraphs.en: Neurons can change connections with their neighbors over time, but this usually happens on the scale of days or months. Behavior, however, needs to adapt in seconds. A significant number of neuroscientists now believe these large-scale wave patterns may help to reorganize the brain in real time to meet the behavioral demands of waking life.
paragraphs.zh: 神经元可以随时间改变与相邻神经元的连接，但这通常是以数天或数月为尺度发生的。 然而，行为需要在几秒钟内适应。 如今，许多神经科学家相信，这些大规模的波模式可能有助于大脑实时重组，以满足清醒生活中的行为需求。

sents.en: Neurons can change connections with their neighbors over time, but this usually happens on the scale of days or months.
sents.zh: 神经元可以随时间改变与相邻神经元的连接，但这通常是以数天或数月为尺度发生的。

sents.en: Behavior, however, needs to adapt in seconds.
sents.zh: 然而，行为需要在几秒钟内适应。

sents.en: A significant number of neuroscientists now believe these large-scale wave patterns may help to reorganize the brain in real time to meet the behavioral demands of waking life.
sents.zh: 如今，许多神经科学家相信，这些大规模的波模式可能有助于大脑实时重组，以满足清醒生活中的行为需求。

paragraphs.en: “Even if the traveling wave was just the result of neurons firing, like the sound of the engine, it still tells us something very interesting about the brain based on what the person is doing,” Jacobs said. “If you see a sound moving in a direction across your engine, it means something in your engine is directionally organized.”
paragraphs.zh: 雅各布斯说：“即使行波只是神经元放电的结果，就像引擎的声音，它仍然能根据这个人正在做的事情，告诉我们一些关于大脑的非常有趣的信息。如果你听到一个声音在引擎的某个方向上移动，这说明你的引擎中存在某种按方向组织的东西。”

paragraphs.en: As far back as the 1920s , neuroscientists have been measuring the brain’s oscillating electrical activity with electrodes on the surface of the scalp via electroencephalography (EEG). When we pay attention, remember, or sleep, the large-scale frequency of the brain’s electrical activity changes. These various oscillations are commonly known as alpha, beta, gamma, and theta waves, and are measured in hertz.
paragraphs.zh: 早在20世纪20年代，神经科学家就开始通过脑电图（EEG）技术，用放置在头皮表面的电极来测量大脑的振荡电活动。 当我们集中注意力、进行记忆或入睡时，大脑电活动的大尺度频率会发生变化。 这些不同的振荡通常被称为α波、β波、γ波和θ波，并以赫兹为单位进行测量。

sents.en: As far back as the 1920s , neuroscientists have been measuring the brain’s oscillating electrical activity with electrodes on the surface of the scalp via electroencephalography (EEG).
sents.zh: 早在20世纪20年代，神经科学家就开始通过脑电图（EEG）技术，用放置在头皮表面的电极来测量大脑的振荡电活动。

sents.en: When we pay attention, remember, or sleep, the large-scale frequency of the brain’s electrical activity changes.
sents.zh: 当我们集中注意力、进行记忆或入睡时，大脑电活动的大尺度频率会发生变化。

sents.en: These various oscillations are commonly known as alpha, beta, gamma, and theta waves, and are measured in hertz.
sents.zh: 这些不同的振荡通常被称为α波、β波、γ波和θ波，并以赫兹为单位进行测量。

paragraphs.en: But recording electrical activity from outside the skull limits the fidelity of the information you can gather. Jacobs’ lab specializes in intracranial brain recordings. People with severe epilepsy may have had electrodes placed inside their brain to help locate the source of their seizures. With roughly 100 electrodes placed in a particular brain region, and with permission from the patient, Jacobs and his team are able to capture high-resolution data — across both space and time — as the participants perform various thinking tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 但是从颅骨外记录电活动会限制你所能收集信息的保真度。 雅各布斯的实验室专门从事颅内脑电记录。 患有严重癫痫的人可能在大脑内植入了电极，以帮助定位其癫痫发作的源头。 通过在大脑特定区域放置约100个电极，并在患者的许可下，雅各布斯及其团队能够在受试者执行各种思维任务时，捕获空间和时间上均为高分辨率的数据。

sents.en: But recording electrical activity from outside the skull limits the fidelity of the information you can gather.
sents.zh: 但是从颅骨外记录电活动会限制你所能收集信息的保真度。

sents.en: Jacobs’ lab specializes in intracranial brain recordings.
sents.zh: 雅各布斯的实验室专门从事颅内脑电记录。

sents.en: People with severe epilepsy may have had electrodes placed inside their brain to help locate the source of their seizures.
sents.zh: 患有严重癫痫的人可能在大脑内植入了电极，以帮助定位其癫痫发作的源头。

sents.en: With roughly 100 electrodes placed in a particular brain region, and with permission from the patient, Jacobs and his team are able to capture high-resolution data — across both space and time — as the participants perform various thinking tasks.
sents.zh: 通过在大脑特定区域放置约100个电极，并在患者的许可下，雅各布斯及其团队能够在受试者执行各种思维任务时，捕获空间和时间上均为高分辨率的数据。

paragraphs.en: Neuroengineer Uma Mohan observed waves traveling across the brain during memory tasks, which could help it switch between functions quickly.
paragraphs.zh: 神经工程师乌玛·莫汉（Uma Mohan）观察到，在记忆任务期间，波会在大脑中传播，这可能有助于大脑在各项功能之间快速切换。

paragraphs.en: Jacobs and his collaborator Uma Mohan , who is now a neuroengineer at the National Institutes of Health, were part of a team that used this technique to observe brain activity during memory tasks. In a study published in Nature Human Behavior in 2024, they described waves moving in opposite directions across the brain’s outermost region, the cortex. “They either go back to front or front to back across the brain,” Jacobs said.
paragraphs.zh: 雅各布斯和他的合作者乌玛·莫汉（Uma Mohan，现为美国国立卫生研究院的神经工程师）所在的团队使用这种技术观察了记忆任务期间的大脑活动。 在 2024 年发表于《自然·人类行为》的一项研究中，他们描述了在大脑最外层区域——皮层上朝相反方向移动的波。「它们要么从后往前，要么从前往后穿过大脑，」雅各布斯说。

sents.en: Jacobs and his collaborator Uma Mohan , who is now a neuroengineer at the National Institutes of Health, were part of a team that used this technique to observe brain activity during memory tasks.
sents.zh: 雅各布斯和他的合作者乌玛·莫汉（Uma Mohan，现为美国国立卫生研究院的神经工程师）所在的团队使用这种技术观察了记忆任务期间的大脑活动。

sents.en: In a study published in Nature Human Behavior in 2024, they described waves moving in opposite directions across the brain’s outermost region, the cortex. “They either go back to front or front to back across the brain,” Jacobs said.
sents.zh: 在 2024 年发表于《自然·人类行为》的一项研究中，他们描述了在大脑最外层区域——皮层上朝相反方向移动的波。「它们要么从后往前，要么从前往后穿过大脑，」雅各布斯说。

paragraphs.en: Jacobs said a good way to understand this result is to think of the waves as showing the direction of information propagation. Visual regions are in the back, and the prefrontal cortex, the “higher-level” memory region, is at the front. If you’re paying attention to what you are looking at, signals are traveling backward from receptors in your eyes to the visual cortex, and then forward into the rest of the brain via the wave to form a memory. “The signature of that is to see waves going from the back of the brain to the front,” Jacobs said.
paragraphs.zh: 雅各布斯说，理解这一结果的一个好方法是把波看作显示信息传播方向的指标。 视觉区域在大脑后部，而前额叶皮层——这个“更高层次”的记忆区域——位于大脑前部。 如果你正在关注自己所看的东西，信号会从眼睛中的感受器向后传到视觉皮层，然后通过波向前传递到大脑的其余部分以形成记忆。“这一过程的特征就是可以看到波从大脑后部传向前部，”雅各布斯说。

sents.en: Jacobs said a good way to understand this result is to think of the waves as showing the direction of information propagation.
sents.zh: 雅各布斯说，理解这一结果的一个好方法是把波看作显示信息传播方向的指标。

sents.en: Visual regions are in the back, and the prefrontal cortex, the “higher-level” memory region, is at the front.
sents.zh: 视觉区域在大脑后部，而前额叶皮层——这个“更高层次”的记忆区域——位于大脑前部。

sents.en: If you’re paying attention to what you are looking at, signals are traveling backward from receptors in your eyes to the visual cortex, and then forward into the rest of the brain via the wave to form a memory. “The signature of that is to see waves going from the back of the brain to the front,” Jacobs said.
sents.zh: 如果你正在关注自己所看的东西，信号会从眼睛中的感受器向后传到视觉皮层，然后通过波向前传递到大脑的其余部分以形成记忆。“这一过程的特征就是可以看到波从大脑后部传向前部，”雅各布斯说。

paragraphs.en: “We thought that was a way the brain was exploiting this organization to switch between encoding and recall memory functions on a rapid timescale, depending on what you need your brain to be supporting,” Mohan explained.
paragraphs.zh: “我们认为，这是大脑利用这种组织结构，根据大脑当前需要支持的功能，在快速时间尺度上切换编码和回忆记忆功能的一种方式，”莫汉解释道。

paragraphs.en: The 2026 research from Jacobs and Das complicated this picture. It showed that these waves can take on much more diverse shapes, patterns, and ripples, far beyond those created by simple up-and-down and back-to-front movement.
paragraphs.zh: Jacobs 和 Das 在 2026 年的研究使这一图景变得复杂。 研究表明，这些波可以呈现出更加多样的形状、模式和波纹，远远超出了由简单的上下和前后运动所产生的形态。

sents.en: The 2026 research from Jacobs and Das complicated this picture.
sents.zh: Jacobs 和 Das 在 2026 年的研究使这一图景变得复杂。

sents.en: It showed that these waves can take on much more diverse shapes, patterns, and ripples, far beyond those created by simple up-and-down and back-to-front movement.
sents.zh: 研究表明，这些波可以呈现出更加多样的形状、模式和波纹，远远超出了由简单的上下和前后运动所产生的形态。

paragraphs.en: We thought that was a way the brain was exploiting this organization to switch between encoding and recall memory functions on a rapid timescale.
paragraphs.zh: 我们认为，这是大脑利用这种组织结构来在快速时间尺度上切换编码与回忆记忆功能的一种方式。

paragraphs.en: Uma Mohan, National Institutes of Health
paragraphs.zh: Uma Mohan，美国国立卫生研究院

paragraphs.en: In the experiment, the team asked participants to perform two memory tasks. The first was a simple verbal memory exercise, in which they had to recall words they had seen on a screen. The second was a more complex spatial task: They navigated a virtual environment and had to recall the locations of objects they encountered.
paragraphs.zh: 在实验中，研究团队要求参与者完成两项记忆任务。 第一项是简单的言语记忆练习，参与者需要回忆他们在屏幕上看到过的词语。 第二项是更复杂的空间任务：参与者在一个虚拟环境中导航，并需要回忆他们遇到过的物体的位置。

sents.en: In the experiment, the team asked participants to perform two memory tasks.
sents.zh: 在实验中，研究团队要求参与者完成两项记忆任务。

sents.en: The first was a simple verbal memory exercise, in which they had to recall words they had seen on a screen.
sents.zh: 第一项是简单的言语记忆练习，参与者需要回忆他们在屏幕上看到过的词语。

sents.en: The second was a more complex spatial task: They navigated a virtual environment and had to recall the locations of objects they encountered.
sents.zh: 第二项是更复杂的空间任务：参与者在一个虚拟环境中导航，并需要回忆他们遇到过的物体的位置。

paragraphs.en: With the high-resolution method, Jacobs and Das observed two new classes of waves in awake humans for the first time. One, emanating from an area of the cortex, was a concentric wave, like the ripples from a pebble dropped into a lake, or the reverse, in which waves converged on one region. The other was a rotating spiral wave traveling in a clockwise or counterclockwise direction, like a hurricane or a flushing toilet.
paragraphs.zh: 通过这种高分辨率方法，雅各布斯和达斯首次在清醒的人类身上观察到两类新的波。 其中一类是从大脑皮层某个区域发出的同心波，就像投入湖中的石子激起的涟漪；或者是相反的情况，即波向一个区域汇聚。 另一类是以顺时针或逆时针方向传播的旋转螺旋波，就像飓风或抽水马桶的水流一样。

sents.en: With the high-resolution method, Jacobs and Das observed two new classes of waves in awake humans for the first time.
sents.zh: 通过这种高分辨率方法，雅各布斯和达斯首次在清醒的人类身上观察到两类新的波。

sents.en: One, emanating from an area of the cortex, was a concentric wave, like the ripples from a pebble dropped into a lake, or the reverse, in which waves converged on one region.
sents.zh: 其中一类是从大脑皮层某个区域发出的同心波，就像投入湖中的石子激起的涟漪；或者是相反的情况，即波向一个区域汇聚。

sents.en: The other was a rotating spiral wave traveling in a clockwise or counterclockwise direction, like a hurricane or a flushing toilet.
sents.zh: 另一类是以顺时针或逆时针方向传播的旋转螺旋波，就像飓风或抽水马桶的水流一样。

paragraphs.en: “We see the rotating wave in the spatial task a little bit more often than the waves we see in the verbal task, which tend to have a simpler structure,” Jacobs said. “This seems to suggest these rotating waves are better for performing more complex memory behaviors.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们在空间任务中看到旋转波的频率略高于在言语任务中看到的波，后者往往具有更简单的结构，”雅各布斯（Jacobs）说。“这似乎表明，这些旋转波更适合执行更复杂的记忆行为。”

paragraphs.en: Researchers have been making intracranial recordings in humans for a long time, Jacobs said, but they often only looked at one electrode at a time, or a handful. This gave an impression of simple waves across the whole outer cortex. Jacobs realized that, if you look at groups of electrodes that are separated by the right distances, the structure and directionality of the waves becomes clearer.
paragraphs.zh: 雅各布斯说，研究人员在人类颅内进行记录已经很长时间了，但他们往往一次只观察一个电极，或者少数几个电极。 这给人一种整个外层皮层上只有简单波形的印象。 雅各布斯意识到，如果你观察以合适距离分隔的电极群，这些波的结构和方向性就会变得更清晰。

sents.en: Researchers have been making intracranial recordings in humans for a long time, Jacobs said, but they often only looked at one electrode at a time, or a handful.
sents.zh: 雅各布斯说，研究人员在人类颅内进行记录已经很长时间了，但他们往往一次只观察一个电极，或者少数几个电极。

sents.en: This gave an impression of simple waves across the whole outer cortex.
sents.zh: 这给人一种整个外层皮层上只有简单波形的印象。

sents.en: Jacobs realized that, if you look at groups of electrodes that are separated by the right distances, the structure and directionality of the waves becomes clearer.
sents.zh: 雅各布斯意识到，如果你观察以合适距离分隔的电极群，这些波的结构和方向性就会变得更清晰。

paragraphs.en: Mathematical biologist Bard Ermentrout thinks that simple wave patterns seen in past experiments might have been part of more complex waves.
paragraphs.zh: 数学生物学家巴德·埃门特劳特（Bard Ermentrout）认为，过去实验中观察到的简单波型可能是更复杂波的一部分。

paragraphs.en: Jacobs got in touch with Bard Ermentrout , a mathematical biologist at the University of Pittsburgh who had been looking at similar patterns in mice. Ermentrout thinks the simple wave patterns observed in the past might actually have been part of more complex waves. However, until recently, researchers haven’t had access to electrodes placed in the right locations or at the right spatial scale to catch the larger pattern.
paragraphs.zh: 雅各布斯联系了匹兹堡大学的数学生物学家巴德·埃尔门特劳特，后者一直在研究小鼠身上类似的模式。 埃尔门特劳特认为，过去观察到的简单波模式实际上可能是更复杂波的一部分。 然而，直到最近，研究人员才有机会获得放置在正确位置或正确空间尺度上的电极，以捕捉更大的模式。

sents.en: Jacobs got in touch with Bard Ermentrout , a mathematical biologist at the University of Pittsburgh who had been looking at similar patterns in mice.
sents.zh: 雅各布斯联系了匹兹堡大学的数学生物学家巴德·埃尔门特劳特，后者一直在研究小鼠身上类似的模式。

sents.en: Ermentrout thinks the simple wave patterns observed in the past might actually have been part of more complex waves.
sents.zh: 埃尔门特劳特认为，过去观察到的简单波模式实际上可能是更复杂波的一部分。

sents.en: However, until recently, researchers haven’t had access to electrodes placed in the right locations or at the right spatial scale to catch the larger pattern.
sents.zh: 然而，直到最近，研究人员才有机会获得放置在正确位置或正确空间尺度上的电极，以捕捉更大的模式。

paragraphs.en: “Maybe the planar waves are just the outer arms, where you’re missing the eye of the storm,” Ermentrout, a co-author of the April 2026 paper, said. “In a hurricane you only feel the wind going in one direction. You don’t know that it is spinning unless you’re right there by the eye.”
paragraphs.zh: “也许平面波只是外围的旋臂，你错过了风暴之眼，”2026年4月那篇论文的合著者埃门特劳特（Ermentrout）说。“在飓风中，你只能感受到朝一个方向吹的风。 除非你就站在风暴眼的旁边，否则你不会知道它在旋转。”

sents.en: “Maybe the planar waves are just the outer arms, where you’re missing the eye of the storm,” Ermentrout, a co-author of the April 2026 paper, said. “In a hurricane you only feel the wind going in one direction.
sents.zh: “也许平面波只是外围的旋臂，你错过了风暴之眼，”2026年4月那篇论文的合著者埃门特劳特（Ermentrout）说。“在飓风中，你只能感受到朝一个方向吹的风。

sents.en: You don’t know that it is spinning unless you’re right there by the eye.”
sents.zh: 除非你就站在风暴眼的旁边，否则你不会知道它在旋转。”

paragraphs.en: Because the research only collects data from locations where the patients have had electrodes placed as part of their epilepsy treatment, “we might be missing how ubiquitous these patterns really are,” Jacobs said.
paragraphs.zh: 由于该研究仅从患者因癫痫治疗而植入电极的部位收集数据，Jacobs 表示：“我们可能低估了这些模式的普遍程度。”

paragraphs.en: Although there is no consensus yet about what these waves in the brain’s local electric field may be doing, some scientists believe they provide another avenue for the brain to coordinate activity between regions. Miller said that these wave patterns are much more dynamic and flexible than the stable, more architectural connections between neurons. For Miller, it makes sense that the brain would exploit this emergent, biophysical layer of organization that shifts and moves on the same timescale as behavior.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管对于大脑局部电场中的这些波可能在起什么作用尚未达成共识，一些科学家认为它们为大脑在不同区域之间协调活动提供了另一条途径。 米勒说，这些波形模式比神经元之间稳定且更具结构性的连接要动态和灵活得多。 对米勒来说，大脑会利用这个涌现的、生物物理层面的组织是说得通的，因为它的变化与移动和行为处于相同的时间尺度上。

sents.en: Although there is no consensus yet about what these waves in the brain’s local electric field may be doing, some scientists believe they provide another avenue for the brain to coordinate activity between regions.
sents.zh: 尽管对于大脑局部电场中的这些波可能在起什么作用尚未达成共识，一些科学家认为它们为大脑在不同区域之间协调活动提供了另一条途径。

sents.en: Miller said that these wave patterns are much more dynamic and flexible than the stable, more architectural connections between neurons.
sents.zh: 米勒说，这些波形模式比神经元之间稳定且更具结构性的连接要动态和灵活得多。

sents.en: For Miller, it makes sense that the brain would exploit this emergent, biophysical layer of organization that shifts and moves on the same timescale as behavior.
sents.zh: 对米勒来说，大脑会利用这个涌现的、生物物理层面的组织是说得通的，因为它的变化与移动和行为处于相同的时间尺度上。

paragraphs.en: “The architecture of the brain is really important, and the traveling waves tend to follow the anatomy, but they don’t strictly follow it. … The connectivity is more like the information that’s baked into the brain for long-term storage, and the waves are when that information gets expressed in terms of thought and neural processing,” Miller said.
paragraphs.zh: 「大脑的结构确实非常重要，行进波往往会沿着解剖结构传播，但并不严格遵循它。……连接更像是烙印在大脑中用于长期存储的信息，而这些波则是该信息以思维和神经处理形式得到表达的体现，」米勒说。

paragraphs.en: The waves might be relevant to a variety of brain functions. Studies have found evidence that they play a role in sensory processing, prediction, and modulating the underlying excitability of neurons, making them more or less likely to fire when called upon.
paragraphs.zh: 这些脑波可能与多种大脑功能有关。 研究已发现证据表明，它们在感觉处理、预测以及调节神经元潜在兴奋性方面发挥作用，使神经元在被调用时更容易或更不容易放电。

sents.en: The waves might be relevant to a variety of brain functions.
sents.zh: 这些脑波可能与多种大脑功能有关。

sents.en: Studies have found evidence that they play a role in sensory processing, prediction, and modulating the underlying excitability of neurons, making them more or less likely to fire when called upon.
sents.zh: 研究已发现证据表明，它们在感觉处理、预测以及调节神经元潜在兴奋性方面发挥作用，使神经元在被调用时更容易或更不容易放电。

paragraphs.en: Zhiwen Ye, a neuroscientist at Shenzhen Medical Academy of Research and Translation, and his colleagues observed rotating waves that were mirrored across the left and right hemispheres of mouse brains.
paragraphs.zh: 深圳医学科学院的神经科学家叶志文及其同事观察到了在小鼠大脑左右半球之间呈镜像对称的旋转波。

paragraphs.en: A paper published in Science in June 2026 echoes the results found in human epilepsy patients by Jacobs and his team. The neuroscientists Zhiwen Ye of Shenzhen Medical Academy of Research and Translation and Nicholas Steinmetz of the University of Washington also observed circular, rotating waves, but this time in the brains of mice. Fascinatingly, these waves were mirrored and synchronized between the left and right hemispheres. What’s more, in the somatosensory cortex — where information from the senses is integrated with bodily movements — axonal neurons were wired together in a spiraling, circular arrangement. That might facilitate the production of these hurricane-like waves.
paragraphs.zh: 2026年6月发表在《科学》杂志上的一篇论文与Jacobs及其团队在人类癫痫患者中发现的结果相呼应。 深圳医学科学院的叶智文和华盛顿大学的Nicholas Steinmetz这两位神经科学家也观察到了环形旋转波，但这次是在小鼠的大脑中。 令人着迷的是，这些波在左右半球之间呈镜像且同步。 更有甚者，在体感皮层——感觉信息与身体运动在此整合的区域——轴突神经元以螺旋状的环形排列相互连接。 这可能有助于产生这类飓风般的波。

sents.en: A paper published in Science in June 2026 echoes the results found in human epilepsy patients by Jacobs and his team.
sents.zh: 2026年6月发表在《科学》杂志上的一篇论文与Jacobs及其团队在人类癫痫患者中发现的结果相呼应。

sents.en: The neuroscientists Zhiwen Ye of Shenzhen Medical Academy of Research and Translation and Nicholas Steinmetz of the University of Washington also observed circular, rotating waves, but this time in the brains of mice.
sents.zh: 深圳医学科学院的叶智文和华盛顿大学的Nicholas Steinmetz这两位神经科学家也观察到了环形旋转波，但这次是在小鼠的大脑中。

sents.en: Fascinatingly, these waves were mirrored and synchronized between the left and right hemispheres.
sents.zh: 令人着迷的是，这些波在左右半球之间呈镜像且同步。

sents.en: What’s more, in the somatosensory cortex — where information from the senses is integrated with bodily movements — axonal neurons were wired together in a spiraling, circular arrangement.
sents.zh: 更有甚者，在体感皮层——感觉信息与身体运动在此整合的区域——轴突神经元以螺旋状的环形排列相互连接。

sents.en: That might facilitate the production of these hurricane-like waves.
sents.zh: 这可能有助于产生这类飓风般的波。

paragraphs.en: “What we found was there is a circuit, a connection of cells to form these waves, to mediate these waves,” Ye said. “If they are not important, why would the brain try to wire these cells in this way?”
paragraphs.zh: “我们发现存在一个环路，即细胞之间的一种连接，用以形成这些波、介导这些波，”Ye说。“如果它们不重要，大脑为什么要以这种方式将这些细胞连接起来呢？”

paragraphs.en: In a review paper published in September 2026 in Neuron , lead authors Lyle Muller of the University of Texas at Dallas and John Reynolds of the Salk Institute for Biological Studies drew on decades of neuroscientific findings to make the case that traveling waves in the visual cortex could help with predicting upcoming sensory information . They described how evolving patterns can carry information about what the brain has just experienced alongside what it is experiencing now to help the brain make short-term predictions about what it is likely to experience next.
paragraphs.zh: 在2026年9月发表于《Neuron》的一篇综述论文中，第一作者、德克萨斯大学达拉斯分校的莱尔·马勒（Lyle Muller）和索尔克生物研究所的约翰·雷诺兹（John Reynolds）基于数十年的神经科学研究成果提出论点：视觉皮层中的行波可能有助于预测即将到来的感觉信息。 他们描述了不断演变的模式如何既携带大脑刚刚经历的信息，又携带其正在经历的信息，从而帮助大脑对接下来可能经历的内容做出短期预测。

sents.en: In a review paper published in September 2026 in Neuron , lead authors Lyle Muller of the University of Texas at Dallas and John Reynolds of the Salk Institute for Biological Studies drew on decades of neuroscientific findings to make the case that traveling waves in the visual cortex could help with predicting upcoming sensory information .
sents.zh: 在2026年9月发表于《Neuron》的一篇综述论文中，第一作者、德克萨斯大学达拉斯分校的莱尔·马勒（Lyle Muller）和索尔克生物研究所的约翰·雷诺兹（John Reynolds）基于数十年的神经科学研究成果提出论点：视觉皮层中的行波可能有助于预测即将到来的感觉信息。

sents.en: They described how evolving patterns can carry information about what the brain has just experienced alongside what it is experiencing now to help the brain make short-term predictions about what it is likely to experience next.
sents.zh: 他们描述了不断演变的模式如何既携带大脑刚刚经历的信息，又携带其正在经历的信息，从而帮助大脑对接下来可能经历的内容做出短期预测。

paragraphs.en: The waves in the local electric field may play a key role in cognition, Miller said, with the ability to excite or inhibit the underlying neural machinery. He describes neurons in the cortex as “Humpty Dumpty sitting on a wall,” teetering right on the edge of firing. This oscillating electrical activity can alter the voltage gradient at the synapses that connect neurons, making them more or less likely to fire in the future.
paragraphs.zh: 米勒说，局部电场中的波可能在认知中发挥关键作用，因为它们能够兴奋或抑制底层的神经机制。 他将皮层中的神经元描述为「坐在墙上的蛋壳先生」，正处于放电的临界边缘摇摇欲坠。 这种振荡的电活动可以改变连接神经元的突触处的电压梯度，使它们在未来更容易或更不容易放电。

sents.en: The waves in the local electric field may play a key role in cognition, Miller said, with the ability to excite or inhibit the underlying neural machinery.
sents.zh: 米勒说，局部电场中的波可能在认知中发挥关键作用，因为它们能够兴奋或抑制底层的神经机制。

sents.en: He describes neurons in the cortex as “Humpty Dumpty sitting on a wall,” teetering right on the edge of firing.
sents.zh: 他将皮层中的神经元描述为「坐在墙上的蛋壳先生」，正处于放电的临界边缘摇摇欲坠。

sents.en: This oscillating electrical activity can alter the voltage gradient at the synapses that connect neurons, making them more or less likely to fire in the future.
sents.zh: 这种振荡的电活动可以改变连接神经元的突触处的电压梯度，使它们在未来更容易或更不容易放电。

paragraphs.en: Not everyone buys the hypothesis that traveling waves in the local electric field play a role in how the brain processes information. For György Buzsáki , a systems neuroscientist at New York University, waves are merely a reflection of what’s going on underneath, at the synaptic level. The more neurons you have, and the more synchronous they are, the stronger the electrical field and the oscillations in it will be. The patterns can tell us interesting things about the circuitry underneath, but that’s about it, according to Buzsáki. “The current that is being generated is done by synapses,” he said. “When current goes into the neuron, they do their computation and generate their action potentials and communicate with each other. You don’t need anything happening in the extracellular space.”
paragraphs.zh: 并非所有人都接受“局部电场中的行波在大脑处理信息的过程中发挥作用”这一假设。 对于纽约大学的系统神经科学家捷尔吉·布萨基（György Buzsáki）来说，波仅仅是表层之下、突触层面所发生事情的反映。 神经元数量越多，它们越同步，电场及其中的振荡就会越强。 在布萨基看来，这些模式能告诉我们一些有关底层神经回路的有意思的事情，但也仅此而已。“被产生的电流是由突触完成的，”他说，“当电流进入神经元时，神经元会进行它们的计算，产生动作电位并相互交流。 不需要细胞外空间中发生任何事情。”

sents.en: Not everyone buys the hypothesis that traveling waves in the local electric field play a role in how the brain processes information.
sents.zh: 并非所有人都接受“局部电场中的行波在大脑处理信息的过程中发挥作用”这一假设。

sents.en: For György Buzsáki , a systems neuroscientist at New York University, waves are merely a reflection of what’s going on underneath, at the synaptic level.
sents.zh: 对于纽约大学的系统神经科学家捷尔吉·布萨基（György Buzsáki）来说，波仅仅是表层之下、突触层面所发生事情的反映。

sents.en: The more neurons you have, and the more synchronous they are, the stronger the electrical field and the oscillations in it will be.
sents.zh: 神经元数量越多，它们越同步，电场及其中的振荡就会越强。

sents.en: The patterns can tell us interesting things about the circuitry underneath, but that’s about it, according to Buzsáki. “The current that is being generated is done by synapses,” he said. “When current goes into the neuron, they do their computation and generate their action potentials and communicate with each other.
sents.zh: 在布萨基看来，这些模式能告诉我们一些有关底层神经回路的有意思的事情，但也仅此而已。“被产生的电流是由突触完成的，”他说，“当电流进入神经元时，神经元会进行它们的计算，产生动作电位并相互交流。

sents.en: You don’t need anything happening in the extracellular space.”
sents.zh: 不需要细胞外空间中发生任何事情。”

paragraphs.en: Although the true nature of what, if anything, these waves are doing is not fully settled, evidence is mounting that they may be important to how the brain organizes, processes, and expresses information in real time.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管这些波究竟在做什么（如果它们确实有作用）的真实本质尚未完全确定，但越来越多的证据表明，它们可能对大脑如何实时组织、处理和表达信息非常重要。

paragraphs.en: “Biology exploits regularity and predictability, and these waves are doing organized, predictable things in association with cognitive functions,” Miller said. “If that doesn’t tell you something is going on, I don’t know what does.”
paragraphs.zh: “生物学利用规律性和可预测性，而这些波正在与认知功能相关联地做着有组织的、可预测的事情，”米勒（Miller）说。“如果这还不能告诉你有什么东西在发生，那我不知道什么才能说明这一点了。”
